title: FinOps Tactic Playbook - KB-Aligned Remediation Patterns

relationship_definitions.PRIMARY: Required when the verified finding activates the binding.
relationship_definitions.SUPPORTING: Evaluated by GenAI during category expansion.

tactics.activity_goal: Establish enforceable tagging and allocation controls that connect material cloud spend to a validated owner and allocation dimension, while keeping exceptions visible and time-bound.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows missing, inconsistent, or non-enforced allocation tags.
Material spend cannot be attributed reliably to teams, products, services, or cost centers.
when_not_to_use: Allocation failure is caused mainly by billing-source ingestion or account hierarchy defects.
The organization has no approved ownership or cost-allocation model to encode.
prerequisite_evidence: Tag-key and value coverage by account, service, and spend.
Approved ownership and allocation dimensions.
Examples of policy violations, exceptions, and unallocated spend.
implementation_activities: Define mandatory tag keys, controlled values, scope, and precedence rules.
Map each rule to an accountable owner and allocation outcome.
Implement policy-as-code in audit mode and measure violations before enforcement.
Create remediation, exception approval, expiry, and escalation workflows.
Phase enforcement by risk and report compliance and unallocated spend by owner.
expected_artifacts: Versioned tagging and allocation standard with scope and precedence
Policy-as-code rules and deployment inventory
Time-bound exception register with owners and expiry dates
Compliance and unallocated-spend dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Mandatory rules are approved, versioned, and mapped to allocation outcomes.
Audit-mode results establish a baseline and enforcement scope.
Every active exception has an owner, rationale, expiry date, and review path.
risks_and_controls: Risk: immediate enforcement may block valid deployments. Control: begin in audit mode and phase hard enforcement by tested risk tier.
Risk: compliant tags may still produce incorrect allocation. Control: reconcile tagged allocation to billing totals and ownership records.

tactics.activity_goal: Create a versioned cloud financial policy framework that assigns decision rights and converts approved spend, provisioning, allocation, budget, and exception rules into proportionate controls.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows cloud financial policies are absent, fragmented, contradictory, or non-enforced.
Provisioning and spend decisions lack consistent thresholds, owners, or exceptions.
when_not_to_use: The immediate issue is non-compliance with an already complete and effectively enforced policy.
Decision rights and accountable owners have not been agreed.
prerequisite_evidence: Current policies, approval paths, exception records, and provisioning controls.
Material spend-risk scenarios and delivery constraints.
Decision-authority and ownership model.
implementation_activities: Consolidate current rules and identify conflicts, gaps, and unenforced obligations.
Define policy scope, decision rights, thresholds, required evidence, and control strength.
Specify tag, budget, provisioning, commitment, and exception requirements.
Implement automated feedback, audit checks, and hard gates only where proportionate.
Approve, publish, version, communicate, and review the policy on a defined cadence.
expected_artifacts: Versioned cloud financial policy with scope and decision rights
Approval and escalation matrix with financial thresholds
Control catalog linking each policy clause to detection and enforcement
Exception register with owner, rationale, expiry, and compensating control
acceptance_criteria: Each material policy requirement has an owner, decision right, and measurable control.
Automated and manual enforcement points are documented and tested.
Exceptions are time-bound, reviewable, and linked to compensating controls.
risks_and_controls: Risk: excessive policy friction drives bypass behavior. Control: use proportional guardrails and automated feedback before hard gates.
Risk: policy exists only on paper. Control: map clauses to owners, telemetry, workflow controls, and compliance reporting.

tactics.activity_goal: Bring cloud account and subscription creation into a governed vending process that applies ownership, billing, identity, security, network, logging, and lifecycle controls by default.
when_to_use: Verified evidence identifies shadow accounts, unmanaged subscriptions, or ad hoc account creation.
New accounts are created without consistent owner, billing, or baseline controls.
when_not_to_use: The environment already uses a complete vending process and the finding concerns post-provisioning policy drift.
There is no approved target landing-zone or baseline-control model.
prerequisite_evidence: Complete account and subscription inventory with billing and ownership status.
Approved landing-zone, identity, network, security, logging, and tagging baselines.
Examples of unmanaged-account risks and production dependencies.
implementation_activities: Reconcile provider, identity, billing, and configuration inventories to identify unmanaged scopes.
Define request, approval, ownership, purpose, budget, and lifecycle requirements.
Automate account creation and baseline controls through approved templates.
Register each account in billing, identity, monitoring, and ownership systems.
Risk-rank and migrate unmanaged accounts with workload owners and rollback plans.
expected_artifacts: Reconciled account and subscription inventory with governance status
Account vending workflow and approval contract
Versioned baseline-control template with validation checks
Risk-ranked unmanaged-account migration register
acceptance_criteria: Every active in-scope account has a verified owner, purpose, billing scope, and governance status.
New accounts can be created only through the approved workflow or a recorded exception.
Baseline-control validation passes before account handover.
risks_and_controls: Risk: abrupt closure of unmanaged accounts disrupts production. Control: classify dependencies and migrate with owners using staged cutover and rollback.
Risk: teams bypass a slow vending process. Control: define service targets, automate standard paths, and monitor out-of-band creation.

tactics.activity_goal: Turn approved budgets into progressive, owner-routed controls that prompt timely decisions while protecting production continuity and explicitly governing exceptions.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows repeated budget overruns without accountable response.
Budget alerts exist but lack materiality, owner routing, escalation, or decision records.
when_not_to_use: Budgets are not based on an approved scope, forecast, or ownership model.
Hard enforcement would affect production without a tested service-continuity exception path.
prerequisite_evidence: Approved budgets and scope-to-owner mappings.
Historical variance, seasonality, and response outcomes.
Production criticality and safe enforcement boundaries.
implementation_activities: Define progressive forecast, actual-spend, and materiality thresholds by scope.
Route each threshold to an owner with required response and decision deadline.
Implement escalation stages from notification to approval or bounded restriction.
Restrict automated hard controls to tested, reversible, non-production scopes.
Review variance causes, exceptions, and threshold effectiveness monthly.
expected_artifacts: Budget threshold and materiality policy by governed scope
Owner-routing and progressive escalation matrix
Production-safe enforcement and exception runbook
Variance decision log with corrective actions
acceptance_criteria: Every governed budget has an owner, thresholds, response duties, and escalation path.
Production-impacting controls require an approved exception and continuity check.
Material variances produce a recorded decision, action, or accepted rationale.
risks_and_controls: Risk: hard stops disrupt service. Control: use progressive controls and limit automation to tested reversible scopes.
Risk: static thresholds generate noise. Control: review materiality, seasonality, forecast changes, and alert outcomes regularly.

tactics.activity_goal: Create an evidence-ranked modernization backlog for migrated workloads by comparing current cost and operational constraints with feasible cloud-native alternatives and accountable decision points.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows lift-and-shift workloads retain material legacy cost or operational inefficiency.
Post-migration optimization has not been performed or decisions are undocumented.
when_not_to_use: Workloads are scheduled for near-term retirement or repatriation.
Current cost, dependency, reliability, or owner evidence is insufficient for prioritization.
prerequisite_evidence: Workload cost, utilization, dependencies, criticality, and service objectives.
Migration history and known technical debt.
Owner, lifecycle decision, and delivery constraints.
implementation_activities: Rank migrated workloads by material cost, stability, technical debt, and business criticality.
Assess right-sizing, managed-service, container, serverless, storage, and retirement options.
Estimate value, change effort, reliability risk, and dependency impact for feasible options.
Record optimize, modernize, retain, retire, or defer decisions with owners.
Sequence approved work into a funded backlog with validation and rollback expectations.
expected_artifacts: Risk- and value-ranked post-migration workload backlog
Current-versus-target architecture and cost assessment
Modernization decision records with assumptions and owner
Sequenced delivery roadmap with validation and rollback gates
acceptance_criteria: Priorities combine verified cost, feasibility, reliability, and business criticality.
Each in-scope workload has a documented disposition and accountable owner.
Approved changes include outcome measures, validation gates, and rollback criteria.
risks_and_controls: Risk: modernization cost exceeds achievable value. Control: require option comparison, bounded pilots, and stage-gated funding.
Risk: architectural change degrades reliability. Control: sequence stable high-value workloads and require service-objective validation and rollback.

tactics.activity_goal: Make material cost implications and uncertainty visible before architecture or infrastructure decisions are approved, without presenting estimates as guaranteed forecasts.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows architecture decisions omit cost estimates or financial trade-offs.
Material infrastructure changes are approved without cost ownership or variance thresholds.
when_not_to_use: The decision has no material or differentiating cost impact.
The available design is too incomplete to produce even a bounded directional estimate.
prerequisite_evidence: Proposed architecture, demand assumptions, service objectives, and regions.
Current unit prices, discount assumptions, and comparable actuals where available.
Architecture approval workflow and materiality thresholds.
implementation_activities: Define which decisions require cost analysis and the minimum evidence standard.
Add demand, unit-price, discount, growth, and uncertainty assumptions to design records.
Estimate baseline and alternative scenarios with material cost drivers.
Integrate automated IaC cost deltas and reviewer thresholds where reliable.
Record the approved option, assumptions, owner, and post-deployment validation date.
expected_artifacts: Cost-aware architecture review checklist and evidence threshold
Scenario-based cost estimate with assumptions and uncertainty range
Cost-extended architecture decision record
IaC cost-delta control and post-deployment validation record
acceptance_criteria: Material decisions compare feasible options using consistent assumptions.
Estimate uncertainty and excluded cost drivers are explicit.
Actual post-deployment cost is compared with the approved estimate and variance is explained.
risks_and_controls: Risk: directional estimates are treated as promises. Control: state ranges, assumptions, exclusions, and confidence explicitly.
Risk: cost dominates reliability or security. Control: evaluate cost alongside mandatory non-financial architecture requirements.

tactics.activity_goal: Bound autoscaling cost exposure with workload-specific limits, anomaly escalation, and tested safety mechanisms while preserving agreed reliability objectives.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows autoscaling has unbounded or unjustified maximums and no cost signal.
Scale events have caused material unexpected spend or uncontrolled retry amplification.
when_not_to_use: The workload does not use automatic scaling.
Demand and reliability behavior have not been characterized sufficiently to set safe bounds.
prerequisite_evidence: Scaling policies, observed demand peaks, and scale-event history.
Service objectives, capacity model, and failure behavior.
Unit cost per scaled resource or request.
implementation_activities: Model cost and capacity across expected, peak, and failure-induced scale scenarios.
Set justified minimums, maximums, rate limits, and cost ceiling alerts.
Define escalation and circuit-breaker behavior for abnormal growth.
Test legitimate peaks, runaway demand, retry storms, and capacity exhaustion in staging.
Monitor cost, saturation, availability, and exception use after rollout.
expected_artifacts: Workload-specific autoscaling and financial-guardrail policy
Capacity-to-cost model with approved operating bounds
Peak, failure, and circuit-breaker test evidence
Guardrail exception and post-rollout monitoring record
acceptance_criteria: Scaling bounds are justified by tested demand and reliability scenarios.
Abnormal scale events generate owner-routed cost and operational alerts.
Guardrails preserve approved service objectives in tested peak scenarios.
risks_and_controls: Risk: cost limits cause under-capacity or outage. Control: derive bounds from service objectives and test legitimate peak demand.
Risk: permissive exceptions make limits ineffective. Control: require owner, rationale, expiry, and monitoring for every exception.

tactics.activity_goal: Provide service-owning teams with decision-ready cost views that link spend movement to ownership, operational drivers, budgets, and actions within existing engineering cadences.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows cost data is restricted to finance, administrators, or provider consoles.
Engineering owners cannot explain or act on material service-level cost changes.
when_not_to_use: Source cost data or ownership mappings are too incomplete to support trusted team views.
The main gap is authority to act rather than access to cost information.
prerequisite_evidence: Service-to-team ownership map.
Validated cost and usage data at an actionable granularity.
Current engineering review cadence and user-access constraints.
implementation_activities: Define dashboard decisions, audiences, materiality thresholds, and drill-down paths.
Publish cost by service, owner, environment, trend, budget, and material driver.
Add anomaly context and links to accountable action workflows.
Grant role-based access and embed review into engineering operating cadence.
Measure adoption, unresolved ownership gaps, and actions initiated from the view.
expected_artifacts: Role-based engineering cost dashboard with documented metric definitions
Service and owner mapping with unresolved-gap register
Team cost-review template with decision and action fields
Dashboard adoption and actionability report
acceptance_criteria: Material services have named owners and accessible cost views.
Dashboard totals reconcile to the approved reporting source within defined tolerance.
Engineering reviews record decisions or actions for material variances.
risks_and_controls: Risk: raw spend views create noise or blame. Control: show trends, drivers, ownership, thresholds, and action paths together.
Risk: inconsistent metrics erode trust. Control: publish definitions and reconcile dashboard totals to the governed source.

tactics.activity_goal: Create a governed, reconcilable cost model across providers and billing scopes without discarding provider-specific dimensions needed for audit and optimization.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows fragmented provider, account, or tool-specific cost views.
Cross-cloud allocation or comparison requires a common semantic and unit model.
when_not_to_use: Only one provider and one governed billing source are in assessment scope.
Provider exports are unavailable or cannot be reconciled to invoices.
prerequisite_evidence: Provider billing exports, schemas, currencies, and invoice totals.
Account-to-owner and business-unit mappings.
Known provider-specific discounts, credits, and amortization rules.
implementation_activities: Inventory billing sources, scopes, currencies, refresh cycles, and data owners.
Define a FOCUS-compatible or equivalent canonical cost schema and mapping rules.
Preserve provider-native fields and lineage for drill-down and reconciliation.
Implement currency, credit, discount, and amortization transformations.
Reconcile normalized totals to source exports and publish data-quality exceptions.
expected_artifacts: Versioned canonical cost schema and provider mapping specifications
Provider/account/owner mapping table
Invoice and source reconciliation report with tolerances
Unified reporting layer with provider-native drill-down
acceptance_criteria: All in-scope sources map to the canonical schema with documented exceptions.
Normalized totals reconcile to approved sources within stated tolerance.
Users can trace a normalized value to its provider-native record and transformation.
risks_and_controls: Risk: normalization hides provider nuance. Control: retain provider-native fields and lineage for drill-down.
Risk: currency or discount treatment distorts comparisons. Control: version transformation rules and reconcile each reporting period.

tactics.activity_goal: Detect material cost deviations early and route each actionable signal to a verified owner through a measurable triage and resolution process.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows material cost spikes are discovered only during periodic reporting.
Existing alerts lack owner routing, materiality tuning, or recorded resolution.
when_not_to_use: Cost data latency is longer than the response window the tactic is expected to provide.
Ownership gaps prevent reliable alert routing.
prerequisite_evidence: Historical spend patterns and known seasonality.
Service and owner mapping.
Examples of past anomalies, detection delay, and financial impact.
implementation_activities: Define materiality and sensitivity thresholds by service, environment, and owner.
Configure anomaly detection with seasonality and known-change context where available.
Route alerts to accountable owners with severity, evidence, and response targets.
Implement triage, escalation, closure reason, and false-positive feedback workflows.
Tune thresholds using precision, response time, and realized impact.
expected_artifacts: Versioned anomaly rules and materiality thresholds
Owner-based alert routing and escalation matrix
Triage runbook with response targets and closure reasons
Resolution and tuning log with false-positive metrics
acceptance_criteria: Material anomalies route to a named owner within the defined latency target.
Alerts record acknowledgement, decision, resolution, and closure reason.
Threshold reviews use false-positive rate and missed-impact evidence.
risks_and_controls: Risk: excessive alerts reduce trust. Control: start with material thresholds and tune from recorded outcomes.
Risk: automated detection misreads planned changes. Control: enrich alerts with deployment, budget, and seasonality context.

tactics.activity_goal: Convert verified stable demand into conservatively sized commitments governed by forecast confidence, purchase authority, utilization targets, and renewal controls.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows sustained eligible on-demand usage without a governed commitment strategy.
Existing commitments lack utilization, coverage, ownership, or renewal oversight.
when_not_to_use: Demand is volatile, short-lived, or expected to migrate before the commitment term ends.
Usage eligibility or billing data is not reliable enough to model downside risk.
prerequisite_evidence: Historical eligible usage and spend by region, service, and purchase family.
Demand forecast and known architecture changes.
Current commitment inventory, utilization, expiry, and ownership.
implementation_activities: Segment stable baseline demand and exclude uncertain or non-eligible usage.
Model conservative purchase scenarios with utilization and break-even sensitivity.
Review financial exposure, portability, and architecture risk with accountable owners.
Approve purchases through defined authority and record assumptions.
Monitor coverage, utilization, realized savings, and renewal decisions.
expected_artifacts: Commitment candidate analysis with scenario and sensitivity assumptions
Approved purchase decision record with accountable owner
Coverage, utilization, and realized-savings dashboard
Renewal and expiry calendar with decision lead times
acceptance_criteria: Purchase quantity is supported by stable eligible usage and documented downside analysis.
Approval authority, assumptions, and owner are recorded before purchase.
Utilization and expiry exceptions trigger a defined review action.
risks_and_controls: Risk: over-commitment creates stranded cost. Control: size against conservative baselines and phase purchases.
Risk: architecture change invalidates assumptions. Control: require workload-owner review and pre-renewal reassessment.

tactics.activity_goal: Turn sustained utilization evidence into owner-approved right-sizing changes with workload safeguards, rollback paths, and traceable savings outcomes.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows sustained low utilization, oversizing, or materially inefficient resource shapes.
Provider recommendations exist but are not risk-ranked, actioned, or tracked.
when_not_to_use: Utilization history excludes peak cycles or critical performance indicators.
The workload is scheduled for retirement or modernization before savings can be realized.
prerequisite_evidence: Representative CPU, memory, storage, network, and latency metrics.
Workload criticality, service objectives, and owner.
Current resource cost and change/rollback capability.
implementation_activities: Build a candidate set using sustained utilization and material cost thresholds.
Classify candidates by criticality, peak behavior, dependency, and rollback risk.
Validate recommendations with workload owners and exclude unsupported cases.
Pilot low-risk changes before controlled production rollout.
Measure performance, accepted/rejected/deferred status, and realized savings.
expected_artifacts: Evidence-backed right-sizing candidate register
Workload risk classification and owner decision record
Approved change and rollback plan
Post-change performance and realized-savings log
acceptance_criteria: Every executed change has representative metrics, owner approval, and rollback criteria.
Post-change service objectives remain within approved bounds.
Savings are calculated from validated before-and-after cost rather than recommendations alone.
risks_and_controls: Risk: downsizing harms performance during peaks. Control: include peak windows and service objectives in eligibility tests.
Risk: estimated savings are overstated. Control: record realized cost after change and account for shifted consumption.

tactics.activity_goal: Replace episodic cleanup with governed lifecycle controls that identify ownership, expiry, inactivity, approval, recovery, and recurring waste causes.
when_to_use: Verified evidence identifies idle, orphaned, expired, or permanently unused resources.
Cleanup depends on manual campaigns without repeatable owner and recovery controls.
when_not_to_use: Resource telemetry or ownership data cannot distinguish idle from intermittently required assets.
Retention, legal-hold, or recovery requirements are unresolved.
prerequisite_evidence: Resource inventory with owner, age, activity, and cost.
Workload schedules and retention requirements.
Past cleanup incidents and recovery constraints.
implementation_activities: Define resource-specific inactivity, orphan, expiry, and materiality rules.
Assign owners and classify candidates by operational and retention risk.
Create notification, approval, quarantine, deletion, and recovery stages.
Automate low-risk schedules and expiry controls with exception handling.
Track removed cost, recoveries, exceptions, and recurring creation causes.
expected_artifacts: Risk-ranked waste and orphan inventory
Lifecycle and expiry policy by resource class
Cleanup runbook with quarantine and recovery windows
Time-bound exception and realized-savings register
acceptance_criteria: Deletion candidates meet documented inactivity and ownership checks.
Material removals use approval, quarantine, and recovery controls.
Recurring waste causes are assigned preventive actions, not only cleanup actions.
risks_and_controls: Risk: cleanup removes a needed asset. Control: require owner notification, quarantine, and tested recovery windows.
Risk: retention duties are breached. Control: integrate legal, backup, and data-retention checks before deletion.

tactics.activity_goal: Adopt discounted interruptible capacity only where workload design, retry behavior, fallback capacity, and service objectives make interruption financially and operationally acceptable.
when_to_use: Verified evidence identifies batch, stateless, distributed, or delay-tolerant workloads using only on-demand capacity.
Workload owners can test interruption and fallback behavior.
when_not_to_use: The workload cannot tolerate interruption, checkpoint, retry, or capacity unavailability.
Regulatory or service-level constraints require guaranteed capacity.
prerequisite_evidence: Workload interruption tolerance and recovery design.
Availability objectives, runtime duration, and demand pattern.
Provider interruption history and alternative-capacity pricing.
implementation_activities: Classify workload eligibility using interruption, state, duration, and service-objective criteria.
Design checkpoint, retry, graceful termination, and fallback behavior.
Pilot with bounded capacity in a non-critical or recoverable scope.
Test forced interruption and loss-of-capacity scenarios.
Measure completion reliability, fallback usage, and net realized savings.
expected_artifacts: Workload eligibility and exclusion register
Interruption, retry, checkpoint, and fallback design
Forced-interruption test evidence
Pilot reliability and net-savings report
acceptance_criteria: Eligible workloads meet documented interruption and recovery criteria.
Forced-interruption tests complete within approved service bounds.
Net savings include fallback, retry, and operational overhead.
risks_and_controls: Risk: interruption causes failed work or service impact. Control: restrict eligibility and test checkpoint, retry, and fallback paths.
Risk: savings disappear through retries or fallback. Control: measure net cost per successful workload outcome.

tactics.activity_goal: Assign cloud-cost accountability to service-owning engineering teams together with the visibility, decision rights, support, and feedback needed to improve cost without creating blame.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows cloud cost is treated as a finance-only or central-IT responsibility.
Engineering teams influence spend but lack explicit ownership, metrics, or decision cadence.
when_not_to_use: Teams lack reliable service ownership or actionable cost data.
Leadership intends to transfer accountability without authority, enablement, or support.
prerequisite_evidence: Service-to-team ownership and decision-right mappings.
Actionable team-level cost and operational data.
Existing engineering planning, review, and escalation cadences.
implementation_activities: Define cost responsibilities and decision rights by service and role.
Provide team-level cost, unit, trend, anomaly, and allocation views.
Embed material cost review and optimization decisions into engineering cadence.
Create FinOps coaching, escalation, and platform-support paths.
Track actions, realized outcomes, unresolved blockers, and repeatable wins.
expected_artifacts: Service-level cost ownership and decision-right map
Engineering cost scorecard with governed metric definitions
Cost-review agenda and decision/action register
FinOps enablement and escalation model
acceptance_criteria: Material services have named owners with defined cost decisions and escalation rights.
Teams receive reconciled, actionable cost views in their normal operating cadence.
Accountability reviews record decisions, blockers, and outcomes without using spend alone as performance judgment.
risks_and_controls: Risk: accountability without authority creates blame. Control: pair ownership with visibility, decision rights, enablement, and support.
Risk: teams optimize local spend at system expense. Control: include reliability, product, and shared-platform constraints in decisions.

tactics.activity_goal: Create a decision-oriented cadence connecting finance, engineering, product, and business owners around a shared evidence pack, explicit authorities, and tracked outcomes.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows finance, engineering, and business stakeholders make cloud-cost decisions separately.
Existing FinOps meetings lack required inputs, decisions, owners, or closure tracking.
when_not_to_use: The required cost, forecast, ownership, or action data cannot be prepared reliably.
The forum has no delegated authority or escalation destination.
prerequisite_evidence: Stakeholder and decision-right map.
Recurring decisions, unresolved cross-functional issues, and current meeting outputs.
Governed cost, forecast, variance, anomaly, and action data.
implementation_activities: Define forum scope, decision rights, escalation path, cadence, and participants.
Standardize the pre-read: material variances, forecasts, anomalies, commitments, and open actions.
Use a shared vocabulary and require decision-ready proposals for material items.
Record decisions, owners, due dates, assumptions, and unresolved dependencies.
Review closure rate and retire agenda items that do not produce decisions or learning.
expected_artifacts: FinOps forum charter with scope and decision authority
Standard pre-read and meeting agenda
Decision and escalation log with owners and due dates
Action closure and recurring-blocker report
acceptance_criteria: The forum receives complete required inputs before each review.
Material items end in a decision, assigned action, or explicit escalation.
Overdue actions and recurring blockers are visible to accountable leaders.
risks_and_controls: Risk: the cadence becomes meeting theater. Control: define decision rights, mandatory inputs, outputs, owners, and closure metrics.
Risk: conflicting metrics stall decisions. Control: use governed definitions and reconcile the pre-read before the forum.

tactics.activity_goal: Convert executive interest into an approved FinOps mandate, funded capacity, accountable ownership, and conservative outcome commitments grounded in verified baseline evidence.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows FinOps sponsorship is verbal, unfunded, or lacks decision authority.
Responsibilities and measurable outcomes are unclear across finance, engineering, and business leadership.
when_not_to_use: A funded mandate, operating model, and accountable executive forum already exist.
The proposal depends on unverified savings or an unreliable baseline.
prerequisite_evidence: Verified spend baseline, material gaps, and current operating costs.
Stakeholder responsibilities and decision constraints.
Conservative benefit scenarios and required capability investment.
implementation_activities: Define the mandate, scope, decision rights, services, and executive sponsor.
Quantify the current-state problem using verified spend and control gaps.
Build conservative benefit, cost, capacity, and dependency scenarios.
Define roles, funding, milestones, outcome measures, and governance forum.
Secure a recorded executive decision and establish baseline review dates.
expected_artifacts: Approved FinOps charter with mandate and decision rights
Evidence-grounded business case with conservative scenarios
Funded role, capacity, and RACI model
Milestone and outcome plan with baseline review dates
acceptance_criteria: The mandate, sponsor, funding, roles, and decision forum are explicitly approved.
Benefit claims trace to verified baselines and documented assumptions.
Initial milestones have accountable owners, dates, and measurable outcomes.
risks_and_controls: Risk: inflated savings claims undermine credibility. Control: use conservative scenarios, confidence ranges, and verified baselines.
Risk: approval lacks execution capacity. Control: tie mandate approval to funded roles, milestones, and decision authority.

tactics.activity_goal: Turn material cost incidents and overruns into evidence-based system learning that improves controls, workflows, and design without suppressing early reporting through blame.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows cost incidents trigger individual blame, concealment, or repeated uncorrected causes.
Reviews focus on who acted rather than why controls and signals failed.
when_not_to_use: The issue requires a formal fraud, misconduct, or compliance investigation.
Leaders are unwilling to model non-punitive learning behavior.
prerequisite_evidence: Material cost incidents, timelines, alerts, decisions, and impacts.
Relevant process, architecture, ownership, and control context.
Current incident-review and escalation expectations.
implementation_activities: Define review scope, facilitation rules, evidence standard, and separation from misconduct processes.
Reconstruct the event timeline and distinguish proximate actions from systemic causes.
Identify failed, missing, noisy, or bypassed controls and decision conditions.
Assign preventive improvements with owners, dates, and verification measures.
Share sanitized lessons and track recurring themes across teams.
expected_artifacts: Blameless cost-review standard and facilitation guide
Evidence-based incident timeline and systemic-cause record
Preventive improvement backlog with owners and verification
Sanitized recurring-theme and learning report
acceptance_criteria: Reviews distinguish system conditions from misconduct requiring a separate process.
Each material systemic cause produces an owned preventive action or accepted risk decision.
Repeat events are analyzed against prior corrective actions and control effectiveness.
risks_and_controls: Risk: blameless language masks accountability. Control: assign clear action ownership while avoiding unsupported personal fault claims.
Risk: participants withhold evidence. Control: leaders model learning behavior and separate reviews from disciplinary investigations.

tactics.activity_goal: Measure FinOps through attributable operational and financial outcomes linked to verified baselines, accountable actions, and decision cadence rather than activity volume.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows FinOps reports meetings, recommendations, or gross savings estimates without outcome traceability.
Leaders cannot connect FinOps actions to waste, coverage, unit economics, risk, or realized value.
when_not_to_use: Reliable baselines, metric definitions, and action ownership cannot yet be established.
The proposed KPI is outside FinOps influence or cannot support a decision.
prerequisite_evidence: Validated financial and operational baselines.
Action register with owners and implementation dates.
Governed metric sources, definitions, and reconciliation controls.
implementation_activities: Select a bounded KPI set tied to explicit FinOps decisions and stakeholder outcomes.
Define formula, source, owner, baseline, target, frequency, and attribution rule for each KPI.
Link actions to expected and realized outcomes without double counting.
Publish a monthly scorecard with variance, confidence, and corrective decisions.
Retire activity-only or vanity measures that do not inform action.
expected_artifacts: Governed FinOps KPI dictionary with formulas and owners
Baseline and target approval record
Action-to-outcome attribution register
Monthly outcome scorecard with variance decisions
acceptance_criteria: Every KPI has a reconciled source, formula, baseline, owner, and decision use.
Realized outcomes are separated from forecast, avoidance, and recommendation estimates.
Material variance produces a recorded corrective action or accepted decision.
risks_and_controls: Risk: unreliable baselines damage trust. Control: reconcile and approve baselines before targets are set.
Risk: teams game narrow KPIs or double-count savings. Control: define attribution, counter-metrics, and independent finance review.

tactics.activity_goal: Control storage growth, retention, tiering, snapshot cleanup, and retrieval trade-offs through owner-approved lifecycle rules grounded in observed access patterns and obligations.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows uncontrolled storage growth, stale snapshots, or absent tiering and retention rules.
Material data remains in high-cost tiers without validated access need.
when_not_to_use: Access telemetry, data ownership, retention, legal hold, or recovery requirements are unresolved.
The storage is short-lived and already governed by an effective service lifecycle.
prerequisite_evidence: Storage inventory with owner, age, tier, access pattern, cost, and growth.
Retention, legal-hold, backup, recovery, and data-classification requirements.
Retrieval latency, fee, and availability constraints.
implementation_activities: Classify storage by owner, data class, access pattern, retention, and recovery requirement.
Define tiering, archive, snapshot expiry, deletion, and exception thresholds.
Model retrieval cost and latency before selecting candidates.
Pilot policies on low-risk data and test restore and access behavior.
Automate approved rules and monitor cost, retrieval, exceptions, and compliance.
expected_artifacts: Classified storage inventory with owner and lifecycle state
Versioned lifecycle, retention, and snapshot policy
Tiering business case and restore-test evidence
Retention and retrieval exception register
acceptance_criteria: Lifecycle rules respect approved retention, legal-hold, recovery, and access requirements.
Pilot restore and retrieval tests meet documented service expectations.
Automated actions and exceptions are monitored by owner and measured for realized cost.
risks_and_controls: Risk: tiering or deletion impairs access or compliance. Control: validate access, retention, legal hold, and restore before activation.
Risk: retrieval charges erase savings. Control: model total lifecycle cost and monitor post-tier retrieval behavior.

tactics.activity_goal: Attribute model, token, API, inference, and supporting platform cost to approved products, teams, use cases, customers, and environments using cost metadata that excludes unnecessary prompt or personal content.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows AI spend is visible only as provider, platform, or shared-account totals.
Material AI consumption cannot be traced to an accountable use case or product owner.
when_not_to_use: AI request telemetry or provider billing identifiers cannot be joined reliably.
Attribution would require capturing sensitive prompt content rather than bounded metadata.
prerequisite_evidence: Provider billing exports and model or deployment identifiers.
Application, product, team, use-case, customer, and environment ownership mappings.
Current AI gateway or application telemetry fields and privacy constraints.
implementation_activities: Define allocation dimensions, precedence, shared-cost rules, and privacy boundaries.
Instrument requests with approved owner, product, use-case, environment, and correlation metadata.
Map provider model, deployment, token, API, and platform charges to governed dimensions.
Reconcile attributed totals to provider invoices and quantify unallocated spend.
Publish owner views and review material unallocated or anomalous AI spend.
expected_artifacts: Versioned AI cost-allocation model with precedence and shared-cost rules
Approved request-metadata contract and instrumentation inventory
Token, model, API, and platform cost dashboard by accountable dimension
Invoice reconciliation and unallocated AI spend report
acceptance_criteria: Material AI spend maps to approved dimensions or a quantified unallocated category.
Attributed totals reconcile to provider and platform cost sources within defined tolerance.
Instrumentation captures cost metadata without unnecessary prompt or personal content.
risks_and_controls: Risk: attribution telemetry captures sensitive content. Control: collect bounded identifiers and usage measures, not prompt or response bodies.
Risk: shared platform cost is allocated arbitrarily. Control: document drivers, precedence, exceptions, and reconciliation for each shared-cost rule.

tactics.activity_goal: Control cost per successful AI task through risk-based model routing, context and output budgets, caching, batching, and retry limits validated against task-specific quality and latency thresholds.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows premium models are used by default without task-level justification.
Material AI cost is driven by excessive context, output, retries, low cache use, or inefficient batching.
when_not_to_use: Task quality, safety, and latency have no measurable acceptance standard.
The workload is too low-volume for routing complexity to provide material value.
prerequisite_evidence: Task inventory with quality, safety, latency, and business-criticality requirements.
Model-level token, latency, retry, cache, error, and cost telemetry.
Representative evaluation cases and current routing behavior.
implementation_activities: Classify tasks by complexity, risk, modality, latency, and evidence requirements.
Benchmark eligible models and context strategies on representative evaluation cases.
Define primary and near-equivalent fallback routes with quality and escalation gates.
Set context, output, cache, batch, retry, and premium-route limits by task class.
Roll out incrementally and monitor cost per accepted result, quality, latency, and fallback behavior.
expected_artifacts: Task-classification and model-routing policy
Representative evaluation suite with quality, safety, and latency thresholds
Context, output, cache, batch, and retry budget configuration
Cost-quality-latency and fallback performance scorecard
acceptance_criteria: Each route and fallback meets task-specific quality, safety, and latency thresholds.
Premium routing and escalation conditions are explicit, logged, and reviewable.
Optimization is measured as cost per accepted result, not token price alone.
risks_and_controls: Risk: lower-cost routing reduces quality or safety. Control: enforce representative evaluation thresholds and escalation paths.
Risk: retry or fallback loops increase cost unpredictably. Control: cap attempts, log route transitions, and stop on bounded failure conditions.

tactics.activity_goal: Govern AI consumption with owner-based budgets, quotas, anomaly response, approval thresholds, and a value scorecard that links cost to verified workflow and business outcomes.
when_to_use: Verified evidence shows AI consumption grows without budgets, quotas, owner alerts, or approval thresholds.
High-cost AI use cases continue without evidence of workflow, product, or business value.
when_not_to_use: AI cost cannot yet be attributed to accountable use cases or owners.
Proposed value metrics have no governed data source or decision use.
prerequisite_evidence: Use-case ownership and reconciled cost or usage baseline.
Historical token, request, model, quota, and anomaly patterns.
Verified workflow or business outcome measures and decision rights.
implementation_activities: Define budgets, quotas, materiality thresholds, and growth approvals by use case and environment.
Route spend, token, and usage anomalies to owners with progressive escalation.
Require evidence and approval for premium-model or quota expansion.
Define a bounded value scorecard linking cost to accepted outputs, workflow results, or business outcomes.
Review low-value or high-cost use cases for redesign, routing change, throttling, or retirement.
expected_artifacts: AI budget, quota, and materiality policy by owned use case
Owner alert-routing and progressive escalation configuration
Premium-model and quota-expansion approval workflow
AI value scorecard with governed cost and outcome definitions
acceptance_criteria: Every governed use case has an owner, budget or quota, thresholds, and response path.
Expansion decisions include cost, quality, risk, utilization, and value evidence.
Value measures trace to governed workflow or business outcomes and avoid double counting.
risks_and_controls: Risk: quotas interrupt critical AI workflows. Control: use progressive thresholds, criticality-based exceptions, and tested fallback behavior.
Risk: value scorecards become vanity reporting. Control: require governed outcome definitions, accountable decisions, and periodic retirement review.
